name: Kindergarten
sub: Greetings, numbers, family, food and your first sentences

lessons.title: Greetings
learn: 您好 (nín hǎo) is the respectful hello for elders, teachers and customers. 您 is the polite “you”.

lessons.title: How are you?
learn: Add 吗 (ma) to the end of any statement to make a yes/no question: 你好吗？ = How are you? 呢 (ne) means “and you?”.
items: 我 也 很 好。

lessons.title: What's your name?
learn: Chinese doesn't move question words to the front. Just put 什么 (what) where the answer goes: 你叫什么名字？ = You are called what name?
你 叫 什么 名字？
items: 你 叫 什么 名字？

lessons.title: I am a student
learn: 是 (shì) links two nouns: 我是学生 = I am a student. Verbs never change in Chinese: 我是, 你是, 他是.
items: 他 是 老师 吗？
她 是 我 朋友。

lessons.title: Where are you from?
learn: Add 人 (rén, person) to a country: 美国人 = an American. Compare Korean 사람 and Japanese じん!
我 是 美国 人。
items: 你 是 哪 国 人？
我 是 美国 人。

lessons.title: The other digits
learn: You already know 四, 七, 八, 九 and 十. Here are the rest. Notice 一 (one line), 二 (two lines), 三 (three lines)!
items: 一， 二， 三， 四， 五！
六， 七， 八， 九， 十！

lessons.title: Bigger numbers
learn: 11 = 十一 (ten-one), 20 = 二十 (two-ten), 99 = 九十九. For “two of something” use 两 (liǎng), not 二: 两个.

lessons.title: How many?
items: 你 有 几 个 哥哥？
How many older brothers do you have?

lessons.title: Measure words
learn: Between a number and a noun you need a measure word: 个 (general), 本 (books), 杯 (cups). 三本书 = three books. Korean and Japanese counters work the same way!

lessons.title: How much is this?
learn: In speech, prices use 块 (kuài, yuan) and 毛 (máo, 10 cents): 十块钱 = 10 yuan.

lessons.title: Family members
learn: Family words are often doubled: 爸爸 (dad), 妈妈 (mom), 哥哥 (older brother). The second syllable is light and short.
items: 她 是 我 姐姐。

lessons.title: This is my dad
learn: 的 (de) works like English “'s”: 我的书 = my book. With close family you can drop it: 我爸爸 = my dad.
items: 这 是 我 爸爸。

lessons.title: I have, I don't have
learn: The negative of 有 (have) is always 没有 (méiyǒu), never 不有.
items: I don't have a younger brother.
你 有 姐姐 吗？
Do you have an older sister?
我 家 有 四 口 人。
wǒ jiā yǒu sì kǒu rén.
There are four people in my family.

lessons.title: People
items: 他 是 我 爷爷。
我 有 一 个 孩子。

lessons.title: Here and there
items: 那 是 我 的 书。

lessons.title: I want to eat
learn: Chinese word order is subject + verb + object, just like English: 我吃面条 = I eat noodles. 想 (xiǎng) = would like to.
我 想 喝 咖啡。
items: 我 想 喝 咖啡。

lessons.title: How does it taste?
learn: Describing words don't need 是. Instead add 很 (very, often just a link word): 很好吃 = (it's) tasty. 太…了 = too…!

lessons.title: I like it
learn: Put 不 (bù) before a verb to say no: 不喜欢 = don't like. 不 becomes bú before a 4th tone.
items: 我 不 喜欢 咖啡。

lessons.title: Colors
learn: Colors end in 色 (sè): 红色 = red. Red is the lucky color in China.

lessons.title: Big, small, new, old
items: 这 本 书 很 新。

lessons.title: Animals
learn: Most animals are counted with 只 (zhī): 一只猫 = a cat.
items: 我 有 一 只 猫。

lessons.title: In the classroom
items: 桌子 上 有 一 本 书。
zhuōzi shàng yǒu yì běn shū.
There's a book on the table.

lessons.title: Places
learn: 在 (zài) means “is at / in”: 厕所在哪儿？ = Where is the toilet?

lessons.title: Going places
items: 他 来 我 家。

lessons.title: Today and tomorrow
learn: Time words come near the start, before the verb: 明天我去商店 = Tomorrow I go to the shop.
明天 我 去 商店。
items: 明天 我 去 商店。
I'm going to the shop tomorrow.

lessons.title: Weather
items: 今天 天气 很 好。

lessons.title: Speaking Chinese
items: 我 会 说 一点儿 汉语。
I can speak a little Chinese.
请 再 说 一 遍。
